title: How a jet engine works

steps.say: A jet engine is like a giant hair dryer that pushes an airplane forward. Let's open one up and see how it works!
At the very front is the fan. It spins like a huge windmill and scoops in lots and lots of air.
Next the air goes into the compressor. It squeezes the air into a smaller space, like squishing a balloon. Squeezed air gets hot and full of energy!
In the combustor, fuel is sprayed into that squeezed air and lit, like a campfire that never goes out. The hot gas wants to push outward really fast!
The rushing hot gas spins the turbine, which is like a second windmill. A long shaft connects it back to the fan, so the engine keeps itself going.
Finally the gas shoots out the back through the nozzle. Pushing gas backward pushes the plane forward, just like a balloon zooming around when you let it go!
Let's pull the engine apart to see the whole team in a row: fan, compressor, combustor, turbine and nozzle. Each one does a small job, and together they make a lot of push!

recap: So remember: scoop the air in, squeeze it, light it, spin the turbine, and shoot it out the back. That is how a jet engine flies a plane!
question: What do you think would happen if the fan stopped spinning?
